title: What this archive answers
rule: A cluster is a body of questions the recovered material already answers. Clusters are not the archive's categories: the four A/B/C/D categories in taxonomy.json are about authorship, and this file is about subject matter. A work may appear in several clusters.
queries_counted: Query counts are computed from the buckets below at build time. No page may type a number.

clusters.label: Apostasy, Hell and Divine Justice
clusters.reader_question: I have heard that Islam says you have to be killed for leaving the faith, and that God sends almost everyone to hell forever - is that actually what he says, and what do I do with that?
clusters.one_line: His conditional, self-declared minority reading that the apostasy punishment is part of the Shariah but not operative today, together with his Qur'an-based answer to why hell is for the arrogant and why mercy is not the unconditional forgiveness people assume it is.

clusters.label: Foundational Questions of Belief
clusters.reader_question: Okay, but how would I even know God is real — and isn't it a bit much to say faith is just built into me?
clusters.one_line: The foundational layer only: what kind of thing God is claimed to be (not a 'thing' at all), how a finite being could come to know the Absolute, and the four classical routes by which God's existence is held to be provable.

clusters.label: Atheism, Doubt and Evidence
clusters.reader_question: I believe in God but I can't prove it with science - how is that still rational, and what do I actually say when an atheist demands evidence?
clusters.one_line: How Al-Andalusi answers the atheist demand for evidence: belief without proof, weak versus strong atheism, the fitrah as a non-evidential route to knowledge, and the argument that requiring evidence for everything is itself unevidenced.

clusters.label: Feminism, Gender Justice and Aisha
clusters.reader_question: Do Muslim women need feminism, and how do you answer the claim that the Prophet married a child?
clusters.one_line: His 2016 case that Islam already gave women their rights and that feminism is an imported Western ideology, and his three-part historical refutation of the accusation that marrying Aisha at nine was sexual violence - resting on mortality-driven childhood, moral progressionism, and the classical separation of marriage contract from consummation.

clusters.label: Liberalism, Orientalism and Human Rights
clusters.reader_question: Why do Muslim thinkers argue that liberalism and human rights are a Western import that Muslim societies never actually left behind, and how do I answer someone who disagrees?
clusters.one_line: How the author argues that liberalism, secular human rights and colonial 'value occupation' are one continuing formation inside Muslim societies, and what he says to the liberal and ex-Muslim polemicists he thinks are its agents.

clusters.label: Qur'an Interpretation and Textual Questions
clusters.reader_question: What does the Qur'an actually say, and how do I know who is reading it correctly?
clusters.one_line: How scripture is read: the philological and exegetical case study of Q. 86:5-7, plus short works on the limits of a literal reading, translation and euphemism.

clusters.label: Science, Faith and Scientism
clusters.reader_question: Is it really true that science proves my religion, and if not, what actually happened to Muslim science?
clusters.one_line: The archive's case that scientism is a modern European error distinct from science, that the 'decline' of Muslim science is really a drift into positivism and dependency rather than a war between religion and reason, and that the Qur'an was never meant to be validated by science.

clusters.label: Terrorism, Extremism and Violence
clusters.reader_question: Where does this violence actually come from - is it really Islam, and who is allowed to say so without getting shouted down?
clusters.one_line: His account of why modern jihadist violence emerged - traced to post-colonial Western warfare, secular liberalism and imported methodology rather than to Islamic doctrine - together with the scriptural limits he sets on it and the debates he uses to defend that account.
